title: Hermes Tool Provisioning Manifest
description: Exact, verifiable pins for every tool Hermes manages per-install. One source of truth read by installation/provisioner.py and desktop payload staging. Every tool pins an exact version plus, per target, an exact download URL and its sha256.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema file for editor validation.

schemaVersion.description: Bump when the manifest shape changes.

tools.description: Map of tool name -> a pinned version & per-target artifacts.

version.description: Exact upstream version string (no ranges). Semver, or a bare revision number for upstreams that number builds rather than release them (playwright's chromium).

$comment.description: Notes on why this tool/version/build variant was chosen.

optional.description: A capability nobody asked for is not downloaded until something asks. Optional tools are staged on demand, may declare missing targets, and their absence is not drift.

onPath.description: Whether this tool's bin dir joins the managed PATH. False for artifacts that are not a CLI surface (a browser tree the consumer locates by directory).

python.description: The interpreter version this tool installs. Only 'uv' may carry it: uv IS the installer the pin configures, and python-build-standalone's own checksums travel with it rather than being duplicated here.

extends.description: Tools this one plugs into. One edge, two consequences, both derived rather than restated in code: the tool is INSTALLED after everything it extends (staging may run them), and its bin dir sorts BEFORE theirs on PATH (it exists to supersede a copy they ship). npm extends node for exactly that reason.

requires.description: Tools this one cannot function without. Drives SELECTION only: asking for this tool (--extra, provision_tool) also asks for these, transitively. No install-order or PATH consequence — that is what separates it from 'extends'. agent-browser requires the chromium pair it launches.

files.description: Map of '<platform>-<arch>' targets to their pinned artifact, or to a declared gap saying why no artifact exists there. The single key 'any' replaces the whole map when one artifact serves every target. Otherwise every target is named: a silently absent row and a deliberate gap look identical to a reader, and only one of them is a bug.

target.description: Target architecture for binaries, or 'any' for a target-independent artifact (a source/registry tarball whose bytes do not vary).

targetEntry.description: What this target has: an artifact to download, or a reason there is none. Exactly one — the union makes 'present and missing at once' unrepresentable rather than a rule the runtime has to check.

missing.description: A DECLARED gap. The reason is what separates 'upstream ships no such build' from 'someone forgot a row', and the resolver quotes it when refusing.
Why no artifact exists for this target, in a sentence a user can act on.

url.description: URL from where this artifact can be downloaded from.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex-encoded SHA-256 digest of the downloaded artifact, exactly 64 characters.

also.description: Further archives unpacked into the SAME store entry, after the one above. For an upstream that splits one runtime across several downloads which must end up in one directory: llama.cpp ships its CUDA engine and the cudart DLLs it links against as separate zips, and Windows resolves a DLL from the executable's own directory, so two entries plus a PATH edge cannot substitute. Each is pinned and digest-verified exactly like the primary artifact. Use 'extends' instead whenever the pieces are separable tools.

url.description: URL of an additional archive unpacked into the same entry.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex-encoded SHA-256 digest, exactly 64 characters.
